steps.message:
Build a 9-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation titled "Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities" for policy analysts and climate negotiators, using a data-forward, analytical, and authoritative tone.

The deck opens with a striking title slide establishing scope (1750–2024), then builds from the atmospheric CO₂ milestone through historical emission growth, national comparisons, and regional share shifts. It deepens into per capita inequalities and the 2024 annual change snapshot, before explaining how energy mix drives differences and closing with key takeaways that synthesize the findings.

For the per capita slide (slide 6), use a horizontal bar chart layout showing emissions for the US, Canada, China, EU-27, World average, UK, India, and Chad/Kenya to emphasize the 150× disparity. For the energy mix slide (slide 8), include a small comparison table contrasting France/UK versus Germany/Netherlands on energy sources and per capita CO₂. The regional share shift slide (slide 5) should describe a stacked area or side-by-side comparison visual showing the dramatic change from 1900 to 2024. Reference the appropriate figures (figure_1.jpg through figure_4.jpg) as noted in the slide specifications.

Do not fabricate any data not found in source_brief.md. All statistics, figures, and claims must be grounded in the provided source material.

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

1	# Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities
2	
3	## Source
4	https://climate.nasa.gov/vital-signs/carbon-dioxide/ and Our World in Data — CO₂ and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Global Carbon Budget 2025)
5	
6	## Atmospheric CO₂ Concentration
7	
8	The latest measurement from NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory (February 2026) records atmospheric CO₂ at **429 parts per million (ppm)**. This represents a more than 50% increase from the pre-industrial baseline of approximately 280 ppm. The current level is at least 1.5 times greater than the natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago — a change that took thousands of years then but has occurred in roughly two centuries now. Ground-based and satellite measurements confirm the sharp acceleration, linked primarily to the burning of coal, oil, and natural gas.
9	
10	## Global Emissions Trajectory (1750–2024)
11	
12	Before the Industrial Revolution, CO₂ emissions were negligible. Growth remained relatively slow until the mid-20th century. In **1950**, the world emitted roughly **6 billion tonnes** of CO₂. By **1990**, emissions had nearly quadrupled to over **20 billion tonnes**. Today, global annual emissions from fossil fuels and industry exceed **35 billion tonnes**. While emissions growth has slowed in recent years, they have not yet peaked.
13	
14	![Annual CO₂ emissions by country](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
15	
16	## Who Emits the Most? Country-Level Totals
17	
18	China is the world's largest emitter by a significant margin, producing over 12 billion tonnes annually — more than one-quarter of the global total. The United States peaked near 6 billion tonnes around 2005 and has since declined to roughly 5 billion tonnes. India has risen rapidly to approximately 3 billion tonnes. Europe's share has fallen substantially.
19	
20	| Country / Region | Approx. Annual CO₂ (billion t) | Share of Global | Trend (recent) |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| China | ~12.5 | ~27% | Slight increase |
23	| United States | ~5.0 | ~14% | Declining |
24	| India | ~3.0 | ~8% | Rising |
25	| EU-27 | ~2.7 | ~7% | Declining |
26	| Germany | ~0.6 | ~1.7% | Declining |
27	| United Kingdom | ~0.3 | ~0.9% | Declining |
28	| Brazil | ~0.5 | ~1.4% | Roughly stable |
29	| France | ~0.3 | ~0.8% | Declining |
30	
31	In 1900, Europe and the US accounted for more than 90% of global emissions. By 1950, they still represented over 85%. Today, they account for less than one-third, while Asia — home to nearly 60% of the world's population — produces roughly half of all emissions. Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4%, comparable to international aviation and shipping combined.
32	
33	## Per Capita Emissions: Extreme Inequalities
34	
35	Per capita CO₂ emissions reveal stark global inequalities. The world's highest per capita emitters are major oil-producing nations with small populations (Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait). Among large, populous countries, the US, Australia, and Canada have per capita emissions roughly three times the global average.
36	
37	![Per capita CO₂ emissions over time](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
38	
39	| Country | Per Capita CO₂ (tonnes/year) |
40	|---|---|
41	| United States | ~15 |
42	| Canada | ~13 |
43	| Australia | ~15 |
44	| South Africa | ~8 |
45	| China | ~9 |
46	| EU-27 | ~7 |
47	| World average | ~5 |
48	| United Kingdom | ~4 |
49	| France | ~4 |
50	| India | ~2 |
51	| Kenya | <1 |
52	| Chad / Niger | ~0.1 |
53	
54	The gap between the highest and lowest per capita emitters is approximately **150-fold**: the average American or Australian emits in under two days what the average person in Chad or Niger emits in an entire year. Importantly, countries with similar living standards can differ significantly — France and the UK have much lower per capita emissions than Germany or the Netherlands, largely because of their energy mix (higher nuclear and renewable shares).
55	
56	## 2024 Annual Change in Emissions
57	
58	The 2024 map of annual percentage change in CO₂ emissions shows a mixed picture. The United States and much of Europe recorded declines (roughly −1% to −5%), shown in blue. Russia, parts of Southeast Asia, and several African nations saw increases of +2% to +10% or more, shown in orange and red. Before the Industrial Revolution, CO₂ emissions were negligible. Growth remained relatively slow until the mid-20th century. In **1950**, the world emitted roughly **6 billion tonnes** of CO₂. By **1990**, emissions had nearly quadrupled to over **20 billion tonnes**. Today, global annual emissions from fossil fuels and industry exceed **35 billion tonnes**. While emissions growth has slowed in recent years, they have not yet peaked.

![Annual CO₂ emissions by country](./assets/figure_3.jpg)

## Who Emits the Most? Country-Level Totals

China is the world's largest emitter by a significant margin, producing over 12 billion tonnes annually — more than one-quarter of the global total. The United States peaked near 6 billion tonnes around 2005 and has since declined to roughly 5 billion tonnes. India has risen rapidly to approximately 3 billion tonnes. | United Kingdom | ~0.3 | ~0.9% | Declining |
| Brazil | ~0.5 | ~1.4% | Roughly stable |
| France | ~0.3 | ~0.8% | Declining |

def add_shape(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.line.fill.background()
    if fill_color:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    return shape


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=DARK_TEXT, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    return txBox


def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size=16,
                       color=DARK_TEXT, bold_prefix=True, spacing=Pt(8)):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.space_after = spacing
        p.space_before = Pt(2)
        if bold_prefix and ":" in bullet:
            bold_part, rest = bullet.split(":", 1)
            run_b = p.add_run()
            run_b.text = bold_part + ":"
            run_b.font.bold = True
            run_b.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run_b.font.color.rgb = color
            run_b.font.name = "Calibri"
            run_n = p.add_run()
            run_n.text = rest
            run_n.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run_n.font.color.rgb = color
            run_n.font.name = "Calibri"
        else:
            run = p.add_run()
            run.text = bullet
            run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run.font.color.rgb = color
            run.font.name = "Calibri"
    return txBox


def add_stat_box(slide, left, top, width, height, number, label,
                 num_color=ACCENT_BLUE, bg_color=WHITE):
    shape = add_shape(slide, left, top, width, height, bg_color)
    shape.shadow.inherit = False
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.15),
                                     width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.8))
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = number
    run.font.size = Pt(36)
    run.font.bold = True
    run.font.color.rgb = num_color
    run.font.name = "Calibri"

    txBox2 = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.9),
                                      width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.6))
    tf2 = txBox2.text_frame
    tf2.word_wrap = True
    p2 = tf2.paragraphs[0]
    p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    run2 = p2.add_run()
    run2.text = label
    run2.font.size = Pt(12)
    run2.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
    run2.font.name = "Calibri"

def add_image_safe(slide, path, left, top, width=None, height=None):
    if os.path.exists(path):
        kwargs = {"image_file": path, "left": left, "top": top}
        if width:
            kwargs["width"] = width
        if height:
            kwargs["height"] = height
        slide.shapes.add_picture(**kwargs)
        return True
    return False


def make_table(slide, left, top, width, height, rows, col_widths, header_color=HEADER_BAR):
    tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(len(rows), len(rows[0]), left, top, width, height)
    table = tbl_shape.table
    for ci, cw in enumerate(col_widths):
        table.columns[ci].width = cw
    for ri, row_data in enumerate(rows):
        for ci, cell_text in enumerate(row_data):
            cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            run = p.add_run()
            run.text = str(cell_text)
            run.font.size = Pt(12)
            run.font.name = "Calibri"
            if ri == 0:
                run.font.bold = True
                run.font.color.rgb = WHITE
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = header_color
            else:
                run.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = WHITE if ri % 2 == 1 else VERY_LIGHT
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER if ci > 0 else PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    return tbl_shape

    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text

    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    return txBox

    return txBox

def add_shape(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.line.fill.background()
    if fill_color:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    return shape


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=DARK_TEXT, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    return txBox


def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size=16,
                       color=DARK_TEXT, bold_prefix=True, spacing=Pt(8)):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.space_after = spacing
        p.space_before = Pt(2)
        if bold_prefix and ":" in bullet:
            bold_part, rest = bullet.split(":", 1)
            run_b = p.add_run()
            run_b.text = bold_part + ":"
            run_b.font.bold = True
            run_b.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run_b.font.color.rgb = color
            run_b.font.name = "Calibri"
            run_n = p.add_run()
            run_n.text = rest
            run_n.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run_n.font.color.rgb = color
            run_n.font.name = "Calibri"
        else:
            run = p.add_run()
            run.text = bullet
            run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run.font.color.rgb = color
            run.font.name = "Calibri"
    return txBox

def add_image_safe(slide, path, left, top, width=None, height=None):
    if os.path.exists(path):

        if height:
            kwargs["height"] = height
        slide.shapes.add_picture(**kwargs)
        return True
    return False


def make_table(slide, left, top, width, height, rows, col_widths, header_color=HEADER_BAR):
    tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(len(rows), len(rows[0]), left, top, width, height)
    table = tbl_shape.table
    for ci, cw in enumerate(col_widths):
        table.columns[ci].width = cw
    for ri, row_data in enumerate(rows):
        for ci, cell_text in enumerate(row_data):
            cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            run = p.add_run()
            run.text = str(cell_text)
            run.font.size = Pt(12)
            run.font.name = "Calibri"
            if ri == 0:
                run.font.bold = True
                run.font.color.rgb = WHITE
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = header_color
            else:
                run.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = WHITE if ri % 2 == 1 else VERY_LIGHT
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER if ci > 0 else PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    return tbl_shape

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the Global CO₂ Emissions 9-slide PowerPoint deck."""

import os

SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette — authoritative, data-forward
DARK_BG = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x2A, 0x4A)

ACCENT_RED = RGBColor(0xCC, 0x33, 0x33)

DARK_TEXT = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x2A, 0x4A)
VERY_LIGHT = RGBColor(0xF4, 0xF6, 0xF9)

    RGBColor(0xCC, 0x33, 0x33),  # US - red
    RGBColor(0xE8, 0x6C, 0x00),  # Canada - orange
    RGBColor(0xDD, 0xA0, 0x00),  # China - gold

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH

def add_shape(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.line.fill.background()
    if fill_color:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    return shape


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=DARK_TEXT, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    return txBox


def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size=16,
                       color=DARK_TEXT, bold_prefix=True, spacing=Pt(8)):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.space_after = spacing
        p.space_before = Pt(2)
        if bold_prefix and ":" in bullet:
            bold_part, rest = bullet.split(":", 1)
            run_b = p.add_run()
            run_b.text = bold_part + ":"
            run_b.font.bold = True
            run_b.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run_b.font.color.rgb = color
            run_b.font.name = "Calibri"
            run_n = p.add_run()
            run_n.text = rest
            run_n.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run_n.font.color.rgb = color
            run_n.font.name = "Calibri"
        else:
            run = p.add_run()
            run.text = bullet
            run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
            run.font.color.rgb = color
            run.font.name = "Calibri"
    return txBox

                 num_color=ACCENT_BLUE, bg_color=WHITE):

    shape.shadow.inherit = False
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.15),
                                     width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.8))
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = number
    run.font.size = Pt(36)
    run.font.bold = True
    run.font.color.rgb = num_color
    run.font.name = "Calibri"

    run2.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT

            run.text = str(cell_text)

            if ri == 0:
                run.font.bold = True

add_footer(slide4)

slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_shape(slide5, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, SLIDE_HEIGHT, WHITE)

    y_pos += Inches(0.6)

add_shape(slide5, Inches(6.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(6.0), Inches(4.8), VERY_LIGHT)
add_textbox(slide5, Inches(7.0), Inches(1.6), Inches(5.6), Inches(0.5),

            alignment=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

bars_2024 = [
    ("Asia", "~50%", 5.0, ACCENT_RED),

    ("Africa", "~3\u20134%", 0.4, ACCENT_ORANGE),
    ("South America", "~3\u20134%", 0.4, ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("Other / Intl.", "~10%", 1.0, MED_GRAY),

y_pos = Inches(2.3)
for label, pct, bar_w, color in bars_2024:

add_textbox(slide5, Inches(0.5), Inches(6.5), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.5),

add_footer(slide5)

# ============================================================
slide6 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_shape(slide6, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, SLIDE_HEIGHT, WHITE)
add_header_bar(slide6, "Per Capita Gap: 15 t in the US vs. 0.1 t in Chad \u2014 a 150\u00d7 Disparity")

# Horizontal bar chart data
countries = ["United States", "Canada", "China", "EU-27", "World average", "United Kingdom", "India", "Chad / Kenya"]
values = [15, 13, 9, 7, 5, 4, 2, 0.1]

bar_area_width = Inches(9.0)

for i, (country, val) in enumerate(zip(countries, values)):
